chapter: Politics, bebop and the small-band years
title: How the New York scene changed after the war
summary: Crawford says guys stopped swinging and he had to relearn his approach to music.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now, when you were -- so around the time you were working these bands, you began to go into -- oh, there was one thing I forgot to ask you. Was there much of a difference in the scene, the musical scene in New York, when you got out of the Army as opposed to when you went in? Had things begun to change any?

Yeah. Guys stopped swinging. When I finally noticed came out, I find (inaudible). So I asked somebody, man, why do you all play like that? We was talking about someplace I was playing. Why do you all play with that old bebop? Why better for me to play the way I'm don't you play modern? Say, well, (inaudible) way-out playing. Why do you play the way you play? Making a lot of unnecessary noise and stuff.
So that's all. I finally realized that I learned all over again my approach to music.
